tagline: Sync GitHub PRs and issues with Linear tickets automatically
metaTitle: Linear GitHub Integration: Auto Status Updates on PR Merge
metaDescription: Stop moving Linear issues by hand after every merge. GAIA updates issue status as pull requests open and merge, and tracks PR cycle time. See the setup steps.
intro:
Linear's own GitHub integration links pull requests, branches and commits to Linear issues and moves issue status for you, with no extra tool. Connect it in Linear under Settings > Integrations > GitHub, then put the issue ID (like ENG-123) in the branch name, PR title or PR description; copying the git branch name from a Linear issue does this for you. In each team's workflow settings, choose the status an issue moves to when you copy its branch name or open a draft PR, when a PR opens or review is requested, and when the PR merges (usually Done). You can add rules per target branch, for example In QA on merge to staging and Done on merge to main. A closing word such as "Fixes ENG-123" in the PR description also closes the issue on merge.

If that covers your team, you do not need GAIA for status updates. GAIA is for the work the native integration does not do: steps that cross more tools or need judgment. GAIA's GitHub triggers fire on pull request events, new issues and pushed commits in the repositories you pick, and its Linear triggers fire when an issue is created or updated or a comment is added in a team you pick. A workflow written in plain English then acts with GAIA's GitHub, Linear, Slack and Gmail tools: post a Slack summary of what merged today, draft release notes from the issues closed this week, or turn alert emails into triaged Linear issues.

An example workflow: "When a pull request is merged in acme/api, find the Linear issue IDs in its branch name and title, comment on each issue with the PR link, and post a one-line summary to #releases in Slack."

useCases.title: Auto-update Linear issue status from PR events
useCases.description: When a PR is opened referencing a Linear issue, GAIA moves the issue to 'In Review'. When the PR merges, GAIA marks the issue as 'Done'. The Linear board always reflects actual code state.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from GitHub issues
useCases.description: Bug reports and feature requests filed in GitHub can automatically create corresponding Linear tickets, ensuring engineering backlog and GitHub issue tracker stay in sync.

useCases.title: PR cycle time reporting
useCases.description: GAIA tracks the time from Linear issue creation to GitHub PR merge and generates weekly reports showing cycle time by team member and issue type to identify bottlenecks.

useCases.title: Branch naming convention checks
useCases.description: On a schedule you set, GAIA lists open pull requests in the repositories you choose and flags any whose branch name or title has no Linear issue ID, so untracked work shows up before review.

useCases.title: Release notes generation
useCases.description: When PRs are merged to main, GAIA compiles the linked Linear issues into structured release notes organized by feature area, ready for the changelog or product announcement.

howItWorks.step: Connect GitHub and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your GitHub organization and Linear workspace. Select which repositories and Linear teams to synchronize.

howItWorks.step: Describe the workflow in plain English
howItWorks.description: Pick a GitHub trigger (pull request event, new issue or pushed commit) or a Linear trigger (issue created, issue updated or comment added), then write what GAIA should do, for example "when a PR against main references a Linear issue, comment the PR link on the issue". GAIA runs each step with its GitHub and Linear tools.
Every workflow run is recorded, and GAIA can notify you when it acts. You can also ask GAIA at any time to compare open PRs with Linear issue states and list the mismatches.

faqs.question: How does GAIA link a GitHub PR to a Linear issue?
faqs.answer: GAIA looks for Linear issue IDs in PR titles and branch names (like 'ENG-123' or 'feature/ENG-123-user-auth'). It can also parse PR descriptions for Linear issue URLs. Most engineering teams already use these conventions.

faqs.question: What happens if a PR references multiple Linear issues?
faqs.answer: GAIA updates all referenced Linear issues when the PR status changes. This is common for large PRs that resolve several related issues simultaneously.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync Linear issue fields to GitHub PR labels?
faqs.answer: Not as a live mirror. A workflow on GAIA's Linear issue updated trigger can add or change labels on the linked GitHub PR when an issue changes, using GAIA's GitHub tools. It runs once per event in one direction, so treat it as automation, not two-way sync.

faqs.question: How do I make Linear mark an issue Done when the GitHub PR merges?
faqs.answer: Use Linear's own integration; GAIA is not needed for this. Connect GitHub in Linear under Settings > Integrations > GitHub, open your team's workflow settings and set the PR merge automation to Done. Put the issue ID in the branch name, PR title or description so Linear can link the PR to the issue.

faqs.question: Can Linear change ticket status on release instead of on merge?
faqs.answer: Linear's branch rules let you set a different status per target branch, so a merge to staging can move issues to In QA and a merge to your release or main branch can move them to Done. If a release is a tag or a deploy rather than a merge, GAIA can run a workflow on pushed commits or on a schedule, find the issues that shipped and update them.

faqs.question: How do I get monitoring alerts filed as Linear or GitHub issues automatically?
faqs.answer: Start with your monitoring tool's native integrations: error trackers such as Sentry can create Linear and GitHub issues from alerts. If your alerts arrive by email, GAIA's Gmail trigger can start a workflow on each alert email that checks for an existing open issue and, if there is none, creates a Linear or GitHub issue with the error, service and link.
